one_liner: Firefox's and Servo's Rust CSS style engine; its parallel cascade replaced Gecko's sequential C++ style system in Firefox 57.
what_it_does: Stylo parses CSS, matches selectors against a DOM and computes the cascaded style of every element, including invalidation and restyle after DOM changes. This repository is Servo's downstream sync of the copy in mozilla-central, published as the `stylo` crate (library name `style`) plus `selectors`, `servo_arc`, `stylo_traits`, `stylo_dom` and others. It is not a drop-in library: a host must expose its DOM through the TNode/TElement traits and drive the traversal; the `gecko` feature needs mozilla-central's generated bindings, so only the `servo` flavour builds standalone.
how_it_is_fast: Styling is a top-down tree traversal, so once a parent's style is known its children are independent; Stylo walks the DOM breadth-first and hands chunks of discovered children to a rayon work-stealing pool (rayon in_place_scope_fifo / spawn_fifo in style/parallel.rs and style/driver.rs), staying sequential until a DOM level is wide enough to be worth splitting. Computed styles are split into immutable 'style structs' shared between elements through servo_arc::Arc with copy-on-write mutation. Per-thread caches avoid repeated work: a style sharing cache lets siblings and cousins with identical rule matches reuse a computed style without selector matching, and a counting Bloom filter of ancestors fast-rejects descendant selectors (the same idea as Gecko's AncestorFilter and WebKit/Blink's SelectorFilter); matched rules are inserted into a shared rule tree so elements with the same rule chain share one node.
when_to_use: Building a browser engine, HTML/CSS renderer or document layout tool in Rust that needs browser-grade CSS (cascade, inheritance, media queries, invalidation); crates.io shows Servo's crates and Blitz (blitz-dom, stylo_taffy) as the main dependents.
Styling large documents (thousands of elements, wide DOM levels) on multi-core machines, where the work-stealing traversal can use up to 6 style threads.

Using only the `selectors` crate for CSS selector matching in your own tree type; it is also standalone and far more widely used (about 85 million crates.io downloads versus about 395,000 for `stylo`).
Studying how a production parallel tree traversal is structured in Rust: adaptive sequential-to-parallel switch, per-thread caches, Arc-shared immutable results.
when_not_to_use: As a C++ library: there is no C or C++ API outside mozilla-central's generated Gecko bindings, so a C++ engine cannot simply link it.

Small documents or single-core targets: the traversal stays sequential until a DOM level is wider than the work-unit size, and with one thread or fewer no pool is created, so the parallel gain disappears.

Projects that need a stable API: crate versions break roughly monthly (0.20.0 on 2026-08-04, 0.21.0 on 2026-09-08, 0.22.0 on 2026-09-30) and the main branch is rebased on every upstream sync, so `git pull` does not work across syncs.

Simple stylesheet-to-attribute tasks (inline CSS for e-mail, CSS linting): the engine is large (it replaced about 160,000 lines of C++ with 85,000 lines of Rust, before later growth) and pulls in rayon, cssparser, ICU segmenter and many other crates.

integration.form: crate (stylo 0.22.0, lib name `style`, plus selectors, servo_arc, stylo_traits, stylo_dom, stylo_atoms, stylo_static_prefs and derive crates)
integration.dependencies: rayon, cssparser 0.38, selectors, servo_arc, hashbrown, parking_lot, icu_segmenter, euclid, app_units, smallvec, thin-vec, string_cache and about 30 more crates; `gecko` feature additionally needs bindgen and mozilla-central bindings
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024 (Rust 1.85+); CI builds with current stable; no rust-version field
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows in CI (debug builds and tests; release build on Linux); wasm32 has a no-thread code path; Firefox builds its copy inside mozilla-central
integration.thread_safety: Designed for parallel use: a global rayon pool (default 0.75 x logical CPUs, capped at STYLO_MAX_THREADS = 6, overridable through the layout.threads pref in Servo or layout.css.stylo-threads in Gecko); DOM nodes are not Send and cross threads only through an unsafe SendNode wrapper, with per-element mutable state in AtomicRefCell that panics on conflicting borrows.

gotchas: The only measurement is end-to-end Firefox page load on Amazon's homepage (30%, 2017), Firefox with Stylo against Firefox with the old C++ style system, with no hardware, core count, build flags or run count. It mixes parallelism with the rewrite's other optimisations (style sharing cache, rule tree and Bloom filter tuning), and the old C++ system shipped only in Firefox 56 and earlier (Mozilla wiki snippet), so the comparison cannot be rerun on a current build.

Thread scaling is capped by design: style/global_style_data.rs limits the pool to 6 threads because 'the performance benefit of additional threads seems to level off at around six' (Mozilla bug 1431285 comment 14). The Mozilla Hacks claim of 'up to 2 or 4 or even 18 times faster' (seen only as a search snippet; hacks.mozilla.org is unreachable here) therefore cannot come from thread count alone and has no published method.

The Servo flavour in this repo differs from Firefox's: downstream patches and prefs decide which CSS features are enabled (recent commits switch on writing modes, text-indent keywords and justify-items propagation for Servo), and open issue #235 notes that the default restyle damage 'rebuild_box' is bad for performance.

Off-main-thread styling calls back into host code; the Rust blog post says such calls regularly exposed thread-safety bugs in Firefox's C++ caches and global mutable state, so a host's own callbacks must be thread-safe.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The sibling entries are general runtimes and benchmarks (Rayon vs OpenMP, NPB-Rust, Tokio, Pony, CAF comparisons); pick Stylo only when you need a CSS engine, and treat it as the largest production example of rayon work-stealing applied to an irregular tree traversal. For general data-parallel loops use rayon directly, as in the NPB-Rust and Rayon vs OpenMP entries.
verified_claims_summary: A Rust blog post by Servo/Stylo developer Manish Goregaokar for the Firefox Quantum release (2017-11-14) says parallel styling gave 'a 30% page load speedup for Amazon's homepage' compared with Gecko's earlier sequential C++ style system. Compiler, flags, hardware, core count and number of runs are not given, and no benchmark code exists.
status_note: Very active (daily commits, last 2026-10-11; monthly crate releases), MPL-2.0, shipped to every Firefox user since version 57 and used by Servo and Blitz; usable as a Rust crate if you implement its DOM traits, but the API churns every sync and the performance evidence is a single 2017 first-party number.
